findings.summary: The sticker language is still well below the reference in every app, and the earlier verdict's main gap has not closed. The reference's stickers are large die-cut objects, about 200px, with a deep extruded rim, and they shape the composition at the band edges. Here the hero objects are mostly 100–150px flat line drawings with little or no back face. Every product app has a single header-band sticker of about 60–100px, pushed into the band's top corner and cropped by the side and the top seam, so on desktop it reads as a fragment and on phones only a sliver shows. Of the settings stickers, only the billing token has a real side. The empty-cart drawing reuses the header bag, recoloured. One blog sample has no front-page hero at all, only a compact header band with one cut-off object.
findings.promptFix: A sticker is a thick object, not an outline. Draw the face. Repeat the same shape 10–15% of the object's height lower as its back, in the same fill and outlined in ink. Join the two with the side silhouette so a solid band of edge shows, then add 1–3 inner strokes (rim, fold, seam). A shape with one outline and a hairline edge is not a sticker. The first screen of a front page (home of a publication, store or product site) is a hero band with a hero-size headline and 4–6 different stickers ringing it, never a compact header band. On a hero, at least half the stickers are 160–240px wide on desktop, and no object is drawn twice. A header-band sticker is at least as tall as the band's title block (never under 96px on desktop or 64px on phones). It sits vertically centred at the band's trailing edge, is cropped by that side only (never by the band's top or bottom seam) and shows at least 60% of itself on every viewport. When the band is too short, shrink the sticker or move it inward. An empty state draws the missing thing in its own silhouette and pose, never a recoloured copy of another sticker on the page.

findings.summary: Dark mode reverses the reference's depth on every screen of every app. The page ground is dark grey (#242423) and every card, panel, table, menu, dialog, input and empty box is pure black, where the reference has a black ground with boxes a step lighter. Panels sink instead of rising. The black top bar and footer merge with the panels. Hard shadows (35% white) barely show, so menus, dialogs and the hover lift lose their picked-up depth. Dashed frames fade, and an ink-outlined sticker inside a black box loses its outline. In the same way, the status pill on a colour band turns black in dark because it is filled with `color.surface.raised`. The spec's own dark tokens set this up, and it has not changed since the earlier review.
findings.promptFix: Dark tokens: the page ground `color.surface.default` is #000000 and raised boxes `color.surface.raised` are one step lighter, #242423, edged with the 35% white hairline. Depth then reads as it does in light mode, with white boxes on paper. The top bar and footer stay black fields. A toast, menu or dialog on a black field stays on the raised tone and keeps a visible hard shadow. Anything placed on a colour band (status pill, outline button, chip) keeps its light-mode white fill and ink text in both modes. A sticker keeps its ink outline in both modes, so it sits on a band or raised field, never directly on black.

findings.summary: Content without its own image falls back to a generic picture glyph (sun and mountains, or a photo icon), usually on a flat grey fill. Every product card and product page in commerce does this, and so does every article figure in the blog, where two different subjects share one identical glyph. The reference never shows stock glyphs or grey. Empty media is white with a dashed ink line and a small solid glyph of the thing, and every drawing is a distinct ink-outlined object. Here it is the most visible generic element on the content-heavy screens.
findings.promptFix: When an item has no image of its own (a cover, a product photo, a figure), never draw a generic picture glyph (sun and mountains, a landscape, a photo icon) and never fill the box grey. Do one of two things. Draw the item's own subject as a vignette in the sticker recipe: a band-colour ground with 1–3 flat ink-outlined objects named by the item's topic or kind, different for each item. Or show a `color.surface.raised` box with a 1px dashed ink border and a small solid ink glyph of the item's type.

findings.summary: Several states fall short of their recipe. A successful save shows only a tiny dot and one word instead of the white ink panel on the hard shadow. The busy button turns into a flat grey slab that reads as disabled. Buy-panel options mark the selection with an ink outline or a pill radio instead of the pink selected border on a `radius.sm` box. The empty state's single main action has no plate stack. The reference's states stay drawn: a pink selected border, ink-and-white buttons, and the stacked-plate CTA.

Panel rhythm is looser than the reference's. The password form's fields stop at half the panel width and leave its right half empty. One billing sample leaves a gap below the plan cards about twice the other panel gaps. On some blog pages the band text and body column start far inside the header's logo gutter, so header, band and body sit on different left edges. The reference keeps one edge and even gaps between panels.

Pill rows on phones are cruder than the reference's tidy phone chrome. Section and category pill rows wrap and leave one item alone on a second line, or run off the edge with the last item cut mid-word and no scroll cue. In two settings samples the row sits above the area band and hides the current item off-screen.
A clear glyph inside the focused filter field is drawn in blue, a coloured icon in ink-only chrome.

Phone layout faults. The primary pill nav runs off the screen instead of collapsing into the menu button. Scrolling tables have a sticky first column so narrow that names break one word per line, or clip later columns, flags and status pills at the frame. Breadcrumbs wrap so the separator starts a line. An article's contents row is cut mid-word. A focus ring is clipped by the scrolling row, and an email breaks mid-word in the user menu.

notes: Review: 138/138 checklist items by 8 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/felt-tip-market/0.1.0-rc.1/review-2).
Review: 138/138 checklist items by 8 reviewers and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/felt-tip-market/0.1.0-rc.1/review-2).

The product chrome in all four apps reads clearly as the reference's language and as one family: lemon, periwinkle, teal and marigold header bands closed by black seams, black and white current pills, 1px ink frames on paper, notched pink flags, dashed empty states, the hard-shadow lift and the black footer. Two blog samples also build a real poster hero. What the reference is best known for is still far off: its big, chunky extruded stickers come out as thin line drawings on the hero and as cropped corner fragments in every product app, so the signature score drops below the bar this round. Since the earlier verdict, nothing named there has closed.

Two problems run through every app: dark mode is inverted (grey ground under black boxes), a spec bug in the dark surface tokens, and missing images become stock glyphs on grey. Both make large parts of the output look generic next to the reference. Phone pill rows and tables are also looser than the reference's tidy phone screens, but those are the agents' own layout faults and do not lower the scores.
